bibl.title: From reaction (‘priming’) to motivated selection: changing conceptualizations of accessibility

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: The proposed solution was rather simple: knowledge becomes accessible, which we defined as being ‘functionally available’ to cognitive processes, to the degree that it is motivationally relevant.

span.label: mental accessibility
span.quote: A relevance-based framework for mental accessibility can accommodate results as diverse as ‘saying is believing’ and relevance based- ‘blindness’.

span.label: review
span.quote: With this goal in mind the current paper charts the development of conceptions of mental accessibility from initial ideas of passive ‘spread of activation’ or of bottom-up increase in accessibility to a notion of accessibly that is sensitive to the organism’s current goals, as well as other concerns.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Motivational relevance gates the activation of semantic knowledge, so a stimulus that is not relevant to truth, control or value fails to make its corresponding knowledge functionally available
span.quote: Given that ROAR stipulates that the effect of relevance is on the activation of knowledge, we hypothesized that people were not ‘phenomenally blind’ to the irrelevant percept but rather, could not report what it was

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Feedback that a shared reality failed retroactively lowers the truth relevance of the tuned message, which lowers its accessibility and hence its influence on recall
span.quote: This effect is consistent with the ROAR framework because the later feedback about a failure to create shared reality can still reduce the truth relevance of the message, thereby reducing its accessibility and thus its impact on recall

span.label: The paper deliberately restricts itself to how accessibility has been conceptualised and does not assess whether the hypotheses it reviews are empirically supported.
span.quote: Please note that we focus here on the changing understanding of accessibility that the above hypotheses reflect, which is a separate issue from their empirical verification.

span.label: The authors characterise their own mechanistic model of accessibility as crude.
span.quote: The above examples show that even a crude mechanistic model of mental accessibly that interacts with the motivational relevance of stimuli (from truth, control, or value motivation) can be a promising framework for both predicting and explaining social-cognitive phenomena, as well as cognitive phenomena more generally.

span.label: the priming method and the surrounding cluster of concepts (availability, accessibility, activation, applicability) were imported into social psychology, where their nature was altered to fit social-cognitive phenomena
span.quote: Although the idea of priming per se originated within classic cognitive psychology and psycholinguistics, its nature and the set of related ideas changed when they were applied to phenomena that interested social psychologists.

span.label: accessibility
span.quote: These applications also led to basic models that linked what were then thought to be the sole factors behind the reactivity to information (in the ‘accessibility’ sense of representations acquiring a ‘tendency to be activated’): the frequency and recency of exposure to the information

span.label: applicability
span.quote: Although not fully developed, the key theoretical addition to the mechanics of accessibility in this phase is applicability, which is the precursor to our principle of relevance

span.label: relevance
span.quote: Although not fully developed, the key theoretical addition to the mechanics of accessibility in this phase is applicability, which is the precursor to our principle of relevance

span.label: goals
span.quote: Beyond the additional mental machinery that was added to theories supporting these ideas, the key novel idea was that goals are themselves mental representations that are subject to (more or less) the same principles as other mental representations

span.label: priming
span.quote: For example, although we mentioned above that Bargh and colleagues’ classic study whose findings supported the hypothesis that behavior is directly activated by priming-related concepts failed to replicate, [15] did show that the behavioral outcome of priming

span.label: mental representations
span.quote: Beyond the additional mental machinery that was added to theories supporting these ideas, the key novel idea was that goals are themselves mental representations that are subject to (more or less) the same principles as other mental representations

span.label: accessibility, FIRST GENERATION - a tendency to be activated, fixed by the frequency and recency of exposure and nothing else. Every stage from stimulus to activation is passive and depends only on exposure history, which is exactly why a selective stage had to be added next
span.quote: These applications also led to basic models that linked what were then thought to be the sole factors behind the reactivity to information (in the ‘accessibility’ sense of representations acquiring a ‘tendency to be activated’): the frequency and recency of exposure to the information

span.label: applicability - introduced to solve an OVER-PREDICTION: if accessibility were the whole story every accessible construct would be used, and they are not. Defined as the match between selected features of the stimulus and of the activated concept, and named by these authors as the precursor to their own principle of relevance
span.quote: Although not fully developed, the key theoretical addition to the mechanics of accessibility in this phase is applicability, which is the precursor to our principle of relevance

span.label: accessibility, IN ROAR - redefined from a property fixed by exposure history into one proportional to MOTIVATIONAL RELEVANCE: knowledge is `functionally available` to cognitive processes to the degree that it matters to the organism's current concerns. The same word, with the causal direction reversed
span.quote: The proposed solution was rather simple: knowledge becomes accessible, which we defined as being ‘functionally available’ to cognitive processes, to the degree that it is motivationally relevant

span.label: the paper's own methodological stance, stated once and worth the layer: the CHANGING UNDERSTANDING of a concept is treated as a SEPARATE ISSUE from whether the hypotheses that carried it were empirically verified. That separation is what lets a history of a term be written at all while its results are under dispute
span.quote: Please note that we focus here on the changing understanding of accessibility that the above hypotheses reflect, which is a separate issue from their empirical verification

span.label: builds-on → Higgins' parsing of motivation (reference [24])
span.quote: Building on Higgins’ [24] parsing of motivation we also offered three possible sources of motivational relevance; namely, the mind’s concern with ‘truth’ (what is real), ‘control’ (what I can make happen), and ‘value’ or ‘outcome’ (what is desired/ undesired).

span.label: applicability —same-as→ relevance
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — `PRECURSOR TO`, said by the author of the later principle about the earlier one - which is as close as this corpus gets to a paper identifying its own concept's ancestor. Weighted at 0.8 rather than higher because `precursor` claims descent, not identity, and the schema has no type for that.
span.quote: Although not fully developed, the key theoretical addition to the mechanics of accessibility in this phase is applicability, which is the precursor to our principle of relevance

span.label: relevance —causes→ accessibility
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE REVERSAL THE WHOLE PAPER IS ABOUT. Accessibility stops being a property fixed by how often and how recently something was met, and becomes one proportional to how much it matters to the organism now. Same word, opposite causal direction, thirty years apart.
span.quote: A relevance-based framework for mental accessibility can accommodate results as diverse as ‘saying is believing’ and relevance based- ‘blindness’

span.label: goals —is-a→ mental representations
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The third generation's move: goals are folded INTO the representational machinery rather than added beside it, so everything already true of concept activation becomes true of goal activation without further argument.
span.quote: Beyond the additional mental machinery that was added to theories supporting these ideas, the key novel idea was that goals are themselves mental representations that are subject to (more or less) the same principles as other mental representations

span.label: Merely designating one of two locations as task-relevant produces a blindness to information at the other location, as ROAR predicts.
span.quote: Consistent with the ROAR prediction, a series of experiments [37] showed that merely instructing people that one of two locations is task relevant (e.g. the outer of two differently colored concentric circles) led to ‘blindness’ to the information appearing in the second location (task location).

span.label: Participants who cannot report irrelevant Kanizsa inducers nonetheless see the illusory shape, showing that relevance-based selection acts on knowledge activation rather than on phenomenal experience.
span.quote: This prediction was confirmed in a study in which participants that were ostensibly ‘blind’ (in the sense of non-accessibility) to the inducers of a Kantiza illusion (see Figure 2) nonetheless displayed the illusion by ‘successfully’ judging the orientation of the (relevant) illusory shape

span.label: The shared-reality memory bias is abolished by post-encoding feedback that the shared reality failed, even though encoding conditions were untouched.
span.quote: the biased memory effect disappears when participants are notified just before recall that their reality was not in fact shared by the audience

span.label: Audience tuning alone does not distort recall — the memory bias requires a shared-reality goal, not politeness or ingratiation, despite equal tuning.
span.quote: It does not occur when participants merely tune to be polite or ingratiate their audience [29], despite the degree of audience tuning being at least as great in these cases.

span.label: ROAR (Relevance of Accessible Representations)
span.quote: About six years ago, we outlined a framework that we called ‘ROAR’ for Relevance of Accessible Representations

span.label: accessibility (as functional availability)
span.quote: The proposed solution was rather simple: knowledge becomes accessible, which we defined as being ‘functionally available’ to cognitive processes, to the degree that it is motivationally relevant.

span.label: applicability
span.quote: Applicability was the match between a (select) set of the stimulus’ and the activated concepts’ features

span.label: saying-is-believing effect
span.quote: The ‘saying-is-believing’ phenomenon was discovered by Higgins and Rholes in 1978 and has been recently systematically studied by Higgins, Echterhoff and their colleagues

span.label: irrelevance induced blindness
span.quote: A first demonstration of ‘irrelevance induced blindness’ up to 25% of the participants could not report the color of the single irrelevant concentric circle they had just seen for 500 ms.

span.label: three sources of motivational relevance (truth, control, value)
span.term: three sources of motivational relevance (truth, control, value)
span.quote: Building on Higgins’ [24] parsing of motivation we also offered three possible sources of motivational relevance; namely, the mind’s concern with ‘truth’ (what is real), ‘control’ (what I can make happen), and ‘value’ or ‘outcome’ (what is desired/ undesired).

span.label: up to 25% — share of participants who could not report the colour of the task-irrelevant inner circle
span.quote: For example, up to 25% percent of the participants could not report the color of the (irrelevant) inner circle that was presented for 500 ms without any masking

span.label: 500 ms — unmasked presentation duration of the irrelevant concentric circle that participants still failed to report
span.quote: A first demonstration of ‘irrelevance induced blindness’ up to 25% of the participants could not report the color of the single irrelevant concentric circle they had just seen for 500 ms.
